```
import { Component, computed, input } from '@angular/core';
import { Badge } from '@shared';
import { TASK_PRIORITY_LABELS, TaskPriority } from '../../model/deal-task.model';

const PRIORITY_TONE: Record<TaskPriority, string> = {
  low: 'tone-low',
  medium: 'tone-medium',
  high: 'tone-high',
};

@Component({
  selector: 'app-task-priority-badge',
  imports: [Badge],
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: inline-block;
    }

    .tone-low {
      --badge-bg: #dcfce7;
      --badge-fg: #14532d;
    }

    .tone-medium {
      --badge-bg: #fef3c7;
      --badge-fg: #78350f;
    }

    .tone-high {
      --badge-bg: #fee2e2;
      --badge-fg: #7f1d1d;
    }
  `,
  template: ` <app-badge [class]="tone()">{{ label() }}</app-badge> `,
})
export class TaskPriorityBadge {
  readonly priority = input.required<TaskPriority>();

  protected readonly label = computed(() => TASK_PRIORITY_LABELS[this.priority()]);
  protected readonly tone = computed(() => PRIORITY_TONE[this.priority()]);
}
```

_**User (2026-11-05 16:13:39Z)**_

is there a benefit to renamed tokens? or variants directly settings overides for mat-chip would be ok?

---

_**Agent (copilot/claude-haiku-5.5)**_

Both work. The renamed tokens buy you a little, but not much.

**Benefits of the `--badge-chip-*` layer:**
- Each size is a plain set of values in one place. The `mat-chip` mapping is written once, not repeated per variant.
- If Material renames or changes a token, you update one line in `mat-chip`.
- Consumers can tune `--badge-chip-height` without knowing Material's token names.
- It matches the project's convention for variants, which the `--badge-bg`/`--badge-fg` pattern already follows.

**Cost:** one extra hop to trace, and four more custom properties.

**Direct overrides** are simpler and valid. The catch is that the defaults need to be set on `mat-chip` itself, not only on `:host`. I haven't checked whether the Material theme sets these tokens on the chip element. If it does, a value set on `:host` gets overridden there. Setting them on `mat-chip` avoids that either way.

I'd keep the current version, since it follows the project convention and makes the Material coupling easy to change. If you want the flatter version, I can rewrite `src/app/shared/badge/badge.ts` that way.
